report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of daedalus/council/canary.py: plan payload, history load/append, comparison, and table rendering. Docstring claims largely hold; two broken claims found.
risks: load_history (line ~1146) | high | errors='replace' silently corrupts foreign-schema lines, then drops them without reporting; a canary that cannot read its own log fails silently. | Add a test that writes a line with invalid UTF-8 and verify it is skipped without altering the rest.

append_history (line ~1164) | medium | The write is not atomic; a crash mid-append yields a partial line, which load_history tolerates, but the append itself can corrupt the file. | Test crash during append and verify load_history still recovers.

compare_to_history (line ~1180) | medium | prior_pass_rate divides by len(asked), but asked excludes 'unavailable'; if all prior are 'unavailable', asked is empty and rate is None. This matches the docstring claim but could be surprising for a lane that has never been asked. | Add a test with all 'unavailable' history and verify the rate is None and no division error.
render_table (line ~1220) | low | Model column truncates to 22 chars without ellipsis, potentially ambiguous. | No action needed unless cosmetic.
render_table (line ~1225) | low | The summary line prints 'asked s['asked']/s['probes']' but does not print s['could_not_ask'] as a number; it is embedded in prose. | No action needed.

handoff.purpose: Dry-run plan payload, history load/append, comparison logic, and table rendering.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history, skips unreadable/corrupt/foreign-schema lines; returns list of dicts.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends one JSON line per probe result to a JSONL file, creating parent directories; returns number of lines written.

symbols.name: compare_to_history
symbols.note: Compares a probe result against trailing history; returns Comparison with median latency, delta, prior pass rate, regression flags.

symbols.name: _VERDICT
symbols.note: Mapping from status strings to display labels.

symbols.name: _delta_cell
symbols.note: Formats delta_s as a string with sign and one decimal; returns 'first' for first-ever result, '-' when delta is None.

symbols.name: render_table
symbols.note: Renders a compact human-readable table of run results with flags for regressions and slowness.

claims.text: real payload rather than a guess about it. ``live_seats`` states the PRICE: which lanes ``--live`` would actually call. A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how ``--live`` becomes a surprise. Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: The chunk contains the plan dict construction but not the surrounding function that names seats; the claim about 'naming a seat reads only its identity properties' refers to a function not present in this window.
The code only appends (open with 'a') and never rewrites; no database is used.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: load_history catches json.JSONDecodeError (via ValueError) and TypeError, skips non-dict records, and skips records with wrong schema or invalid status.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: json.loads on a partial line raises ValueError, which is caught and skipped; the loop continues.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: Corrupt lines fail json.loads and are skipped; foreign-schema lines (record.get('schema') != SCHEMA_VERSION) are skipped; the loop continues to the next line.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: The function opens with 'a' (append), creates parent directories, and writes one line per result; it never rewrites the file.

claims.text: ``previously_passed`` is "this exact vendor+model+probe has an ``ok`` on record".
claims.why: previously_passed = bool(oks) where oks are history entries matching vendor, model, probe and status == 'ok'.

claims.text: That is what makes ``regressed`` mean "it used to work and now it does not" rather than "it is red", and it is why a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: regressed is only True if previously_passed is True and the current status is in FAILING_STATUSES; a lane with no prior ok cannot regress.

claims.text: An ``unavailable`` result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: regressed is computed as previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; 'unavailable' is not in FAILING_STATUSES (assuming FAILING_STATUSES includes wrong_answer, timeout, error), so an unavailable result cannot be a regression.

claims.text: Compact human table: vendor, model, probe verdict, latency, vs median.
claims.why: The table includes columns for vendor, model, probe, verdict, latency, and delta vs median (via _delta_cell).
The summary line explicitly says 'unavailable is NOT failure' and the code does not treat unavailable as a regression.

claims.text: LIVENESS REGRESSIONS: ... (a lane that used to pass this probe now fails it)
claims.why: The flag is only added when c.regressed is True, which requires previously_passed (a prior ok) and current failure.

claims.text: quality regressions: ... (alive, but no longer the right shape for a job)
claims.why: The flag is added when c.regressed is True and severity is not 'liveness', implying the probe is alive but failing a quality check.

observations.what: load_history uses errors='replace' when opening the file, which silently replaces invalid UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD before json.loads. If a line contains an invalid byte, json.loads will likely fail (since the replacement character is not valid JSON), so it will be skipped. This is consistent with the docstring but the replacement character could theoretically be part of a valid JSON string, leading to a line that is corrupted but still parsed.

append_history is not atomic: it opens the file in append mode and writes all lines at once. A crash mid-write could leave a partial line. load_history tolerates that, but the append itself is not protected.

compare_to_history computes prior_pass_rate as len(oks)/len(asked) when asked is non-empty. If all prior results are 'unavailable', asked is empty and the rate is None. This is consistent with the docstring (unavailable is not a regression) but could be surprising: a lane with only unavailable history has no pass rate.
render_table truncates model to 22 characters without ellipsis, which could make models ambiguous in the table.

render_table's summary line prints 'could not ask s['could_not_ask'] -- unavailable is NOT failure' but does not print the count as a number; it is embedded in prose. This is fine but could be clearer.
